title: First lesson at Picou's house and his fame for High Society
summary: Picou first shooed Joe away, then gave him a little book; his fame rested on playing High Society.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x:
Like Jelly Roll. But I remember the first time he said, "You be at my house at..." My sister lived on Hillary and Saint Bernard in New Orleans, and I could walk to his house where he was living, and that day... The first day he told me to come around there at around 3 o'clock, and I knocked on the door and he stuck his head out: "I can't be bothered now, boy," he said. "I'm busy." And I could hear him hollering in there, and drinking, and glasses going on. "You come back tomorrow."

So I came back the next day, and we sit down. He pulled out a book, some kind of book, a little old book he gave me...
Why did you want to take lessons with Picou?
Well, I didn't necessarily want to take lessons with Picou, but Papa was the one who suggested it. Because Picou was a famous clarinet player.
How famous was he, I mean, compared with...?

Oh, people talked about him all the time, especially "High Society." People would say, "Can you play 'High Society' like Picou?" He's the one that started all the clarinet players. If you couldn't play "High Society," forget it.
